source.title: From Zipf's Law to Neural Scaling through Heaps' Law and Hilberg's Hypothesis

record.tranche_reason: The paper gives a formal result about cross-entropy scaling, but refines the claim to an information-theoretic lower bound under explicit assumptions rather than demonstrating empirical power-law curves.
record.gate_note: Theorem 5 reports a theoretical lower bound on cross-entropy excess under entropy constraints on model size and compute. Empirical exponents and findings attributed to other papers are cited discussion, not this study's results, and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper is purely theoretical. It derives, under stated assumptions, a lower bound on cross-entropy excess for an abstract random measure Q trained on a stochastic process. It trains and measures no language model and fits no loss curves. Its result is a one-sided bound, not the two-sided power law V1 names, so its own results cannot show whether any version holds in real models. Its remarks on Kaplan vs. Hoffmann exponents and parameter counting (V7-relevant) are arguments about others' cited numbers, not its own results.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors derive a chain Zipf ⇒ Heaps ⇒ Hilberg ⇒ neural scaling under explicit assumptions. Theorem 5 gives information-theoretic lower bounds on cross-entropy excess, not exact exponents. They present it as a baseline and admit the compute bound's justification is fragile.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses mathematical derivations for stochastic processes and entropy bounds, rather than empirical sweeps and fitted scaling curves on language models.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 5 derives a lower bound on worst-case expected cross-entropy excess in terms of data t, entropy-bounded model size n and compute c, from a differential Hilberg law. Under assumptions, eq. 38 gives exponent bounds γT ≤ 1−β and γN ≤ (1−β)/β.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Theoretical claim: neural scaling exponents are bounded above by functions of the Hilberg entropy exponent of the data source.

record.problems: The neural-scaling result depends on abstract assumptions, including the differential Hilberg bound and entropy-based proxies for parameter count and compute. The paper itself notes that the compute-bound justification is fragile and that the theorem does not predict exact exponents. No empirical model evaluation is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Numerical exponents and comparisons attributed to other studies in Sections 2.3 and 3.3 were not extracted because they are cited findings, not results produced by this paper.

untested.parts: No empirical loss measurements. The theorem gives only a lower bound on excess cross-entropy for abstract processes, not a power-law fit for models.
Discusses parameter count as an imperfect capacity proxy and exponent disagreement across cited studies, but tests no fitting choices itself.

missing.what: Derived exponent inequalities γT ≤ 1−β and γN ≤ (1−β)/β, and the argument that Kaplan's γN>γT seems to contradict Theorem 5, possibly because raw parameter count misrepresents information capacity. These are theoretical, not empirical.
missing.locator: Section 3.3, 'Bound on the parameter count' and 'Inequalities and interactions', eq. 38

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' is downgraded: no empirical results on language models, and a one-sided bound on an abstract Q cannot support or challenge V1. The empirical exponent comparisons (Kaplan, Hoffmann, Takahira, Michaud) are cited, not produced here.

versions.untested_parts: No empirical held-out loss curves or separate power-law fits in parameters, tokens, and compute; the theorem concerns an abstract cross-entropy bound under stated assumptions.

rows.subject: random probability measure Q
rows.size_stated: parameter amount n; constrained by H(Q) ≤ A_H^- n
rows.operation_detail: Derives a lower bound on expected cross-entropy excess from a differential Hilberg-law assumption and entropy bounds for model size and compute.
rows.measure: expected cross-entropy rate excess over h
rows.value: Theorem 5, inequality (34): a lower bound on the excess, expressed as A_H^- times the maximum of a term involving t and c and a term involving n.
rows.locator: Theorem 5, inequality (34); Section 3.1 discussion of implications
rows.note: This is a theoretical lower bound, not a measured loss curve or a fitted power law. The authors state that the theorem does not predict exact empirical scaling exponents.
rows.check: The subject is an abstract random probability measure Q under entropy assumptions, not a language model. The value is a derived theoretical lower bound (Theorem 5, eq. 34), not a measured loss. It does not measure what V1 names, so it should be linked to no version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
